context: 思い通りの寸法にいかなくて、やり直す【こと】になった。
english: It didn't go according to plan, so I had to redo it.
note: part of the construction 'こと に なる' (to come to be that, to be decided that)

context: 応接室でお待ち【ください】。
english: Please wait in the reception room.
note: This is an imperative form of くださる, but the entry is for the verb itself. The marked word is an inflected form.

context: 大凡の見積もりを出して【ください】。
english: Please give me a rough estimate.
note: This is an imperative form of くださる, but the entry is for the verb itself. The marked word is an inflected form.

context: 家主が留守の間、隣の人が家の様子を見て【くれた】。
english: While the homeowner was away, the neighbor kept an eye on the house.
note: This is the past tense form of くれる.

context: 再三注意したが聞いて【くれなかった】。
english: I warned him repeatedly, but he wouldn't listen.
note: This is the negative past tense form of くれる.

context: おじいちゃんにプレゼントした湯呑みを、毎日大事に使って【くれて】いる。
english: My grandfather uses the teacup I gave him as a gift every day, taking good care of it.
note: This is the te-form of くれる.

context: テーブルの脚が一つ【ぐらぐらして】いるので、直さないといけない。
english: One of the table legs is wobbly, so I need to fix it.
note: This is the te-form of ぐらぐらする.

context: 相手を舐めて【かかる】と痛い目にあう。
english: If you underestimate your opponent, you'll pay for it.
note: This 'kakaru' means 'to attack' or 'to challenge', which is a different sense/kanji (掛かる) from the entry's 'to take (time/money)' or 'to cost'.

context: 溺れた子供は救急隊員の懸命【な】処置で蘇った。
english: The drowning child was revived by the paramedic's desperate efforts.

context: 次のスピーカーは海外から来た研究者【だそうだ】。
english: I hear the next speaker is a researcher from overseas.
note: This is the copula 'da' followed by 'souda' (I hear that).
